ownerObservations.text: I think the circle for hit damage makes things a little too visually busy, and obscures the meaning of the circle when casting
The flash is maybe a little *too* busy, but this one is definitely the most legible of the 3
This is both easily legible and less busy than the rings
We added outlines to make blue's ice attacks read more easily. The fireballs are also dark in color, or have outlines? This works for legibility but everything looks dirty and unappealing
Yeah I think flash/sparks on hit is the winner. It's both less noisy and more legible

ownerApprovedArtGoal.text: The battle is a visually appealing spectacle with beautiful, coherent, intentional art direction

disposition.chosenTechnique: C: fighter flash and impact sparks for actual damage, rather than damage rings.
disposition.acceptanceScope: Owner explicitly prefers the hit-feedback technique. The complete visual package and ordinary-battle default are not approved by that preference.
disposition.designerRecommendation: Close the hit-versus-cast comparison with C preferred. Scope the proposed follow-up first to the post-engine-refactor appearance of fireballs and ice shards; a whole-scene art redesign was an agent proposal, not the scope of the owner complaint.
remainingConcerns: The duel flash may still be too busy.
The owner finds the post-engine-refactor appearance of fireballs and ice shards dirty and unappealing. This appearance complaint does not concern damage flashes.
Attacker attribution, targeting and fighter identity remain limited.
disposition.implementationStatus: No rendering or gameplay changes in this disposition. Ordinary battle defaults remain as before.
disposition.stoppingCondition: No third ring-versus-flash comparison is needed: the owner chose a technique across the viewed cases. Investigate projectile appearance separately, preserving C hit feedback; broader art direction remains an approved goal rather than an automatically authorized redesign.

futureExperimentDecision.decision: Use hit flashes/sparks in future experiments and retain hit-ring code until a cleanup pass.
futureExperimentDecision.scope: Adopts the hit-feedback technique for future experiments; does not adopt the criticized projectile styling or change ordinary-battle defaults.

factualFollowup.ice: Revised ice uses darker blue material and dark edge lines.
factualFollowup.fireballs: Fire-sphere projectiles use layered colored spheres and trails; the revised ice edge-line branch is not applied to fireballs.
factualFollowup.inspection: Source inspection of BattleView.projectile; no new continuous viewing or visual assessment is claimed.
factualFollowup.causalityLimit: The material/geometry observations describe current code only. They do not establish when or why the post-engine-refactor appearance changed; that requires comparison with pre-refactor rendering.

validation: Documentation-only disposition. Exact feedback copied from retained workspace snapshot; existing rendering/gameplay checks were not repeated against unchanged code.
